purpose: A dated, evidence-bounded review of inputs that might keep metric-v3 development moving after NLM confirmed that previous annual PubMed baselines are not available. This contract does not weaken or replace the original historical-record readiness gate.

decision_rule.original_gate: Only complete, checksummed releases matching the four pinned NLM inventories can satisfy the existing historical-baseline contract.
decision_rule.redesign_gate: A secondary dated snapshot may support a separately pre-registered experiment only after its payload, fixed corpus scope, citation-to-MeSH fields, version date, and limitations are measured and pinned.
decision_rule.current_or_title_abstract_only_data: Current maintained indexing and snapshots without historical MeSH assignments remain engineering or metadata aids only.

alternatives.potential_role: A separately pre-registered pilot over the measured secondary corpus after a successor semantics protocol explicitly handles its observed publication-year scope. It may support post-snapshot discovery cases but is not an NLM baseline substitute.
blockers: The acquired payload matches all three published aggregate counts, but its measured publication-year scope does not match the reported post-1949 scope: 280 records are dated 1946-1949. All years are parseable, although 751,238 values are not plain YYYY.

The 448-record balanced audit is consistent with meshMajor containing all assigned descriptors under maintained-current PubMed: 5,201 of 5,296 assignments match all descriptors and 455 match MajorTopicYN=Y headings. It is not population-weighted, period-appropriate, or evidence of corpus completeness.
The original 416-record protocol remains immutable. Its separately named 448-record successor and checksum-pinned bounded result retain every original threshold and contribute zero readiness.

A separate 21-case secondary-snapshot pilot is frozen before endpoint-support measurement or formula selection. Its five LION cases are source-labelled reproduction targets and its sixteen controls remain ontology-generated proposals, not independently validated discovery truth or verified absences.

The score-free full-snapshot audit found all 21 cases source-compatible at the primary minimum support of 10. However, held-out hard control generated-hard-2012-04-d019956-d019960 has target support exactly 10 and is ineligible at sensitivity 20. The frozen rule says an unevaluable sensitivity is not a pass, so this pilot cannot earn its passing label and does not authorize metric work.

A separately named source-informed successor now preserves all 21 cases and replaces the infeasible sensitivity 20 with sensitivity 5 while keeping primary support 10. It discloses every source count seen before freeze, labels held-out cases score-unseen rather than independent, and remains at zero readiness.

V2's initial formula is frozen before development output: article-level MeSH Jaccard edge weights, minimum aggregation along A-B-C paths, and sum accumulation across B. It is literature-grounded in LION's default but differs materially in graph and co-occurrence unit, retains direct A-C articles, and forbids held-out execution before a final formula freeze.

The initial-formula development measurement is complete for all 11 cases at support 10 and 5, with zero held-out cases computed. None of the three source-labelled positives reaches the top 5%, while three of four ontology-generated hard controls do at both supports. The lower-support run changes no target score or bridge count. This is evidence of poor development discrimination and likely structural-proximity confounding, not held-out validation or a successful gap metric.

The single permitted post-development revision is now checksum-frozen before revision output. It keeps the graph and indirect Jaccard-sum-min score unchanged, divides every candidate score by one plus its exact direct A-C count, consumes the full revision budget, and pre-registers a mechanical development pass-or-terminate gate. It uses no case kind, ontology relation, or held-out metric output; held-out identities and source counts were already known. It contributes zero readiness.
The measured secondary corpus is not the complete 21,508,439-record 2013 NLM baseline, and the two totals are not a measured coverage fraction.
Only a 2013 snapshot is relevant here, so it cannot supply the missing 2007, 2011, and 2012 releases.
Using it changes the experimental population and therefore requires a new pre-registration rather than a source-status flip.
alternatives.next_action: Run the checksum-frozen direct-penalized revision on all 11 development cases at support 10 and 5 into a new refusal-to-overwrite artifact. Apply its pre-registered gate mechanically: pass freezes this exact revision in a separate final contract before one held-out run; failure terminates the pilot without held-out execution. No further formula revision is permitted.
